title.narrative: Provision of Life-Saving Nutrition Services for Vulnerable Communities in Hard-to-Reach Areas of Beletweyne District.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project will be a 12-month integrated nutrition response led by BPHCC, targeting 6,591 individuals directly in seven hard-to-reach villages in Beletweyne District: Buulo Xubey, Shiinle, Lebow, Hodley, Ceelgal, Baslawe and Dolligal. These locations are home to IDPs and vulnerable host communities facing drought, flooding, conflict, displacement, and poor access to essential services. As one of four priority districts under the 2025 SHF Standard Allocation, the intervention will align with SHF’s objectives of life-saving service delivery and integrated response.ltbrgtTo strengthen early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition, BPHCC will engage 14 CHWs, two per village. CHWs will undergo a five-day integrated training covering the IMAM, the Family MUAC approach, and key protection topics including PSEA, AAP, GBV prevention, child protection, and disability inclusion. A separate three-day training on IYCF will build their capacity to deliver nutrition counseling. Trained CHWs will conduct biweekly household visits and train caregivers on Family MUAC to enhance community-based malnutrition screening.ltbrgtMonthly MIYCAN sessions will be conducted in each of the seven villages, promoting exclusive breastfeeding, complementary feeding, dietary diversity, hygiene, and responsive feeding. These sessions will be reinforced by seven care groups—one per village—composed of trained lead mothers. Each lead mother will support neighboring women, creating a peer-to-peer learning model for improved maternal and child nutrition. To enhance household dietary diversity and access to animal-source foods, the project will deliver conditional CVA to 1,712 vulnerable households. Each household will receive a voucher valued at USD 40 to support poultry production under the “One Egg Per Child Per Day” campaign. Vouchers will be redeemable through pre-qualified vendors for chicks, feed, or eggs. Where necessary, in-kind egg donations or poultry support will be provided to care group members lacking poultry assets. Participation in MIYCAN sessions will be mandatory for all CVA recipients, and CHWs will monitor usage and outcomes.ltbrgtThe project will also conduct 28 cooking demonstrations—four per village—delivered in two components. The first will focus on the preparation of enriched nutrient-dense porridge (Tom Brown) using local ingredients. The second will promote egg-based meals, reinforcing the daily inclusion of eggs in children’s diets. Demonstrations will be led by CHWs and care group members to ensure cultural relevance and sustainability.ltbrgtMonitoring and evaluation (ME) will follow Somalia Nutrition Cluster standards. Recent assessments will serve as baselines, and data will be collected monthly using mobile tools, checklists, and interviews. Data will be disaggregated by age, gender, and disability to ensure inclusivity. BPHCC’s ME team and technical staff will oversee data collection and reporting, with quarterly updates submitted to SHF and cluster partners. Community feedback will be gathered via suggestion boxes, home visits, and focus groups to guide adaptive management.ltbrgtProtection and accountability will be fully integrated. CHWs will disseminate AAP principles and manage complaints and feedback mechanisms. BPHCC will coordinate with WARDI to refer 80 children from the stabilization center for child protection and GBV services through the inter-agency referral system. A Protection Officer will manage follow-up and ensure support is provided. The project will actively promote inclusion of marginalized and minority groups. Mapping will identify underserved communities, and tailored strategies will ensure their participation in activities and decision-making processes. Communication materials will be adapted for accessibility, and disaggregated data will be used to monitor equity. BPHCC will also prioritize recruitment of minority staff to reflect community diversity and ensure inclusive delivery of services.ltbrgtlt/pgt
